newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem intervenes in customs service.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem intervenes in customs service.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem said Tuesday he was intervening in the customs service, appointing a special administrator to probe corruption and merge the body with the taxation department.
"I have ordered that this organization be intervened, granting broad administrative and investigative powers to the special administrator," Menem said in a televised address to the nation.
Menem said he had named Carlos Silvani, head of the DGI tax department, as the customs service's administrator.
"I ask all Argentines to continue supporting us in this authentic crusade to combat corruption," Menem said.
The government believes corrupt customs officials have set up a "parallel customs service" to smuggle in goods worth $10 billion -- costing the state $3 billion in lost duties.

Police have raided customs offices, supermarkets and banks in recent days, seizing goods and documents. Seven people have been arrested, including one customs official and six customs "fixers", and 10 others are on the run from the police.
